findings.suggestedFix: Replace all '49' with '51' and 'remaining 46' with 'remaining 48' in Research Findings, US-003 description, and Acceptance Criteria. Add AC: 'No two tasks[] entries share the same id.'
findings.resolution: Updated task counts to reflect verified grep result (51 total, 48 remaining after US-002 ports 3) in Research Findings, US-003, Risk Areas, and Acceptance Criteria; added a no-duplicate-id AC.

findings.sectionRef: Research Findings > Codebase Context; Approach > Files to Create/Modify
findings.description: Plan's line range for the inline JSON block is wrong. Plan states 'roadmap-data JSON: 2180-3529' and 'Inline JS: 3530-3767'. Verified: <script type="application/json" id="roadmap-data"> spans lines 2180-2612 (closing </script> at line 2612). Main inline <script> block runs lines 2614-3767. If implementer follows the stated range literally, the deletion in US-001 would also delete most of the main script. Highest-risk error in the plan.
findings.suggestedFix: Update plan to: JSON block 2180-2612, main inline JS 2614-3767. Update US-001 'DELETE: <script type="application/json" id="roadmap-data"> block (2180-2612, ~430 lines)' (not ~1350).
findings.resolution: Corrected line ranges throughout the plan: JSON block is 2180–2612 (~430 lines) not 2180–3529 (~1350 lines), and inline JS is 2614–3767 not 3530–3767. Updated Research Findings bullets and US-001 deletion in Files to Create/Modify.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Data schema; Approach > Implementation Strategy (US-001)
findings.description: Proposed schema wraps generatedAt/generatedFromCommit under meta:{...}, but the existing consumer at plans/overview.html line 3540 reads data.generatedFromCommit (top-level), not data.meta.generatedFromCommit. As written, US-001 would break the SHA-in-header and freshness-hint features unless the consumer is also rewritten in the same story.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose ONE: (a) keep generatedAt + generatedFromCommit at top level of OVERVIEW_DATA alongside tasks/phaseTree/runs/etc; or (b) introduce the meta:{} wrapper and rewrite the consumer at line 3540 within US-001. Recommend (a) for minimum-change.
findings.resolution: Replaced meta:{} wrapper with top-level generatedAt/generatedFromCommit in the schema, Plan #3 contract, and US-001 strategy — preserves existing overview.html:3540/3543 consumers without same-story rewrite.

findings.description: kanbanCards[] schema with {column, titleHtml, subHtml} is insufficient for identical rendering. Verified: plans/overview.html has 33 .card-meta blocks with rich content (pills, icons, links, inline <code>), and at least one card carries class="card closed" (extra class beyond .card). Inline-style border-color and opacity already documented. The current 3-field schema cannot round-trip card-meta, additional card class names, or inline pills.
findings.suggestedFix:
Widen schema. Option A: kanbanCards[].{column, html} where html is the trusted full inner HTML of
. Option B: structured {column, cardClass: 'closed'|null, titleHtml, subHtml, metaHtml, inlineStyle: string|null}. Recommend A for minimum schema design; render emits
${html}
.
findings.resolution: Widened kanbanCards[] schema to {column, cardClass, inlineStyle, html} (Option A from finding) so rich card-meta content, extra card classes like 'closed', and inline styles round-trip verbatim; updated DOM-contract bullet and renderTasks() emission description to match.

findings.description: phaseTree[] tagged union ({kind: 'task-ref'|'bullet'|'sub-phase'}) is insufficient for identical rendering. Verified: plans/overview.html lines 1920-2009 use .phase-grid, .phase, .phase-head, .item-name with state classes 'open|deferred|donefade|closed', nested <details class="phase-subdetails">, and inline styling. Tagged union can preserve structure but not the state classes or arbitrary inline content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a richer node schema. Each phase: {id, title, headerHtml?, nodes: [{kind:'task-ref'|'raw', taskId?, state?: 'open'|'deferred'|'donefade'|'closed', html?}, ...], subPhases: recursive}. 'raw' carries trusted inner HTML; 'task-ref' carries taskId + state. Render emits the appropriate class names on .item-name.
findings.resolution: Enriched phaseTree schema with state classes, raw-html nodes, headerHtml, and collapsible subdetails to round-trip the actual phase-tree HTML in overview.html:1920–2009; updated Risk Area #3 and US-004 to match.

findings.description: AC promises bookkeeper-workflow updates reflect in 'kanban placement, command-row badge, phase tree pill, and Today panel without further file edits' but does not include an explicit Today-panel verification step. If the data-driven render breaks Today-panel logic (which today walks DOM by class/data-attribute), the AC is unverifiable as a binary pass/fail.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an AC: 'After data-file edit changing a task's phase to impl-in-progress, the Today panel's Running section includes that task within one page reload without console errors. Verified by manual reload on file://.'
findings.resolution: Added explicit Today-panel AC: after data-file edit changing phase to impl-in-progress, single page reload places the task in #today-running with no console errors, confirming buildTodayPanel() still classifies the rendered DOM correctly.

findings.description: AC requires 'same prompt bodies copy-pasteable from the clipboard' but does not specify the decode/re-emit strategy. Risk Areas section identifies HTML-entity decoding as Risk #1 but the AC is silent on implementation. Without an explicit AC, an autonomous implementer may use innerHTML for prompt bodies and re-encode entities, producing copy-paste output that contains '>' instead of '>'.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an AC: 'Prompt bodies in <pre class="cmd-pre"> render with HTML entities decoded to literal characters; render uses textContent (or DOM Node.textContent assignment), not innerHTML, for prompt strings. Verified by manual copy-paste check on first 3 + last 3 tasks: pasted text equals the JS string literal stored in tasks[].command.planPrompt.'
findings.resolution: Plan line 230 already contains an AC matching (and stronger than) the suggested fix: it requires textContent assignment, forbids innerHTML/template-string interpolation, and specifies byte-for-byte copy-paste verification on first 3 + last 3 tasks against tasks[].command.planPrompt. Finding appears to reference an earlier draft.

findings.description: AC says 'Expanding a <details class="cmd"> row, then re-firing the render preserves the open state' but lacks an explicit test procedure or interaction with the existing localStorage 'codexu-overview-details-state-v2' persistence (overview.html line 3106). An implementer might satisfy the snapshot/restore in-render but skip the localStorage re-apply, regressing cross-load persistence.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace with: 'After renderTasks() rebuilds the DOM, all <details class="cmd"> elements that were open before the re-render are still open. Additionally, the existing localStorage codexu-overview-details-state-v2 persistence still works: open 2 details, reload the page, the same 2 are open. Verified manually on file://.'
findings.resolution: Folded into US-002 acceptance criteria in stories-outline.md: open-state snapshot via document.querySelectorAll('details.cmd[open]') before wipe + re-apply by id after render, AND localStorage v2 reload check (open 2 details, reload, both still open).

findings.description: 'Renders identically' is unverifiable in its current form. Codex recommends concrete checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 'renders identically' with: '(1) Kanban column counts match pre-refactor (ready=N, soon=M, blocked=K); (2) Command row count = 51; (3) Every #cmd-<id> hash link jumps to a matching <details>; (4) ?tasks=<id1>,<id2> URL filter shows exactly those tasks; (5) Decoded .cmd-pre text content matches the pre-refactor HTML text content for first 3 + last 3 tasks; (6) Every kanban card retains its .card-meta block.'
findings.resolution: Folded into US-003 'Identical-render check' acceptance criterion (6 concrete checks: kanban column counts, command row count=51, hash-link match, ?tasks= filter behavior, decoded .cmd-pre matches pre-refactor for first/last 3, .card-meta retained); also reflected in plan.md Acceptance Criteria block.

findings.description: Plan says 'add into the existing inline <script> near the top of DOMContentLoaded handling' but plans/overview.html has no DOMContentLoaded wrapper; IIFEs run immediately starting at line 2614. As written, an implementer might add a DOMContentLoaded wrapper that delays render past the IIFE timing.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 'near the top of DOMContentLoaded handling' with 'synchronously at the top of the main inline <script> block (line 2614+), before the first DOM-walking IIFE (PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET / renderPhaseBadges / counts / filters)'.
findings.resolution: Folded into US-002 AC: 'renderTasks() runs synchronously at the top of the main inline <script> (line 2614+), BEFORE the first DOM-walking IIFE (PHASE_TO_ORDER_BUCKET / renderPhaseBadges / counts / filters)'. Plan Architecture section also updated.

findings.resolution: Resolved out-of-band in this conversation session: plans/overview-vite-react.md edited to replace ?id=foo,bar with ?tasks= at lines 66 and 147, and KanbanCard description updated to acknowledge trusted-HTML consumption. Also covered by US-005a 'docs sweep' acceptance criterion and plan AC.

findings.sectionRef: Acceptance Criteria (grep verification); Files to Create/Modify (US-005)
findings.description: Stale-doc sweep target is too narrow. plans/parallel-assignments.md lines 225, 235 say 'bump the lastRanAt timestamp ... in plans/overview.html's roadmap-data JSON'; lines 242, 247 reference 'plans/overview.html roadmap-data JSON' for spawnedFrom and add-new-task instructions. Grepping only for 'edit plans/overview.html' misses these.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand US-005 sweep + AC: grep for each of 'edit plans/overview.html', 'roadmap-data', 'lastRanAt timestamp', 'generatedFromCommit'. Each must be re-pointed at plans/overview-data.js. Update specific lines: plans/parallel-assignments.md 225, 235, 242, 247.
findings.resolution: Folded into US-005a broad-grep AC and plan AC: each of 'edit plans/overview.html', 'roadmap-data', 'lastRanAt timestamp' returns zero hits over .agents/ plans/ packages/ (with plans/overview.html excluded); 'generatedFromCommit' allowed only inside plans/overview-data.js. Stale phrasings at plans/parallel-assignments.md lines 225/235/242/247 named explicitly in US-005a scope.

findings.description: US-005 (docs-and-skill-rewrite) depends on representative-port (Phase 3) so it can run parallel with US-003/US-004. But Risk Areas section #7 says 'write SKILL.md AFTER US-003/US-004 finalize the schema'. Internal contradiction — if US-005 runs parallel with US-003/US-004, the SKILL example snippets would be drafted against the representative-only schema and may need rework once the full port settles.
findings.suggestedFix: Move US-005 to Phase 4, depending on full-task-port AND phase-tree-port. Trades parallelism for correctness. Alternatively: split US-005 into 'US-005a docs-update' (parallel-safe in Phase 3) + 'US-005b SKILL rewrite' (Phase 4, depends on full schema).
findings.resolution: Resolved by splitting US-005 into US-005a (Phase 3 docs sweep, parallel-safe with US-003/US-004) and US-005b (Phase 4 SKILL rewrite, depends on US-003 AND US-004). Suggested-decomposition.json updated with two clusters: docs-sweep and skill-rewrite. Plan's Preliminary Story Decomposition + Suggested Decomposition sections rewritten.

findings.description: US-003 and US-004 both edit plans/overview.html (disjoint line ranges, fine) but both also extend window.OVERVIEW_DATA — US-003 fills tasks[], US-004 fills phaseTree[]. The single top-level object means parallel worktrees both rewrite the same braces. Without an explicit owner of the object skeleton, parallel merge can corrupt the file even if logically additive.
findings.suggestedFix: US-001 creates the full skeleton with empty tasks: [] and empty phaseTree: [] already in place. US-002 fills the 3 representative tasks. US-003 only mutates the tasks: [] array body (append entries). US-004 only mutates the phaseTree: [] array body. Document this 'each story mutates only its array body' invariant in US-003/US-004 stories.
findings.resolution: Folded into US-001 AC (skeleton-ownership invariant stated in the schema-comment block of the data file) and US-003/US-004 ACs each declare 'mutates only its own array body'. Suggested-decomposition.json executionModeRationale strings reference the invariant. The plan's Risk Areas section also documents this isolation.

findings.sectionRef: Suggested Decomposition > full-task-port + phase-tree-port (inline script coordination)
findings.description: Plan's inline render code lives in the same <script> block in overview.html. US-002 adds renderTasks(); US-004 will need to add renderPhaseTree(). The plan does not define explicit section markers, so two parallel worktrees may insert code at adjacent line positions and conflict.
findings.suggestedFix: US-002 inserts BOTH section markers as comments (even if renderPhaseTree() is empty): '// ===== renderTasks() =====' and '// ===== renderPhaseTree() =====' near the top of the inline script. US-004 fills the renderPhaseTree() body inside its marker only. Document this convention in US-002 and US-004 stories.
findings.resolution: Folded into US-002 AC: 'Section markers // ===== renderTasks() ===== and // ===== renderPhaseTree() ===== exist near the top of the inline <script>; US-004 fills the phase-tree marker; this story emits an empty stub.' US-004 AC echoes: 'renderPhaseTree() body lives inside the section marker US-002 emitted; renderTasks() marker is not touched.'

findings.description: AC says 'git grep -n "edit plans/overview.html" .agents/ plans/ packages/ returns zero non-historical hits'. The phrase is ambiguous: plans/overview.html itself contains a self-referential operator-warning comment that legitimately mentions itself. An autonomous verifier could read this AC as failing because of the legitimate hit.
findings.suggestedFix: Clarify AC: 'git grep -n "edit plans/overview.html" -- :!plans/overview.html .agents/ plans/ packages/ returns zero hits' (exclude the file itself from the grep).
findings.resolution: Folded into plan AC: 'git grep -n "edit plans/overview.html" -- :!plans/overview.html .agents/ plans/ packages/ returns zero hits' (plans/overview.html excluded so its own self-warning comment doesn't false-positive). Echoed in US-005a 'narrow grep' AC.

findings.description: AC says 'plans/overview.html no longer contains any kanban <div class="card"> blocks'. After refactor the render JS may legitimately contain card markup as JS string templates, which a naive grep treats as a violation.
findings.suggestedFix: Clarify AC: 'plans/overview.html contains no authored static <div class="card"> elements in the document body; card markup may exist only inside JS string templates or DOM-construction code within the inline <script>.'
findings.resolution: Folded into plan AC and US-003 AC: 'plans/overview.html contains no authored static <div class="card"> elements in the document body (card markup may exist only inside JS string templates or DOM-construction code within the inline <script>).'
